abondances-hsaewal-samiana.summary: The 4 Abundances of Hsæwâl and Samianâ
abondances-hsaewal-samiana.bodyHtml:
Page 24

hôMôh, when his most ardent and sparkling flames burned his coldest and deadliest embrace, separated from Hael two astral Rildées, HSÆWÂL (Vigor / Tolerance / Pleasure / Fidelity) she inheriting his vigorous and adult constitution, then SAMIANÂ (Empathy / Generosity / Poetry / Pity) she enriching herself with his mature and inspired empathy.

  • Before Ô welcomed Hael, they endured with her the fevered burns and deadly frosts of their tormentors. Hsæwâl feasted on insatiable famine upon her juicy and sweet Physrils ( Growing Forms / Plants ) caused by her harvests scorched when Môh was aflame. Samianâ, dependent on her herds of Zoosrils ( Moving Forms (of them- selves ) / Animals), submitted to the frozen pastures of Môh when refrigerated.
  • Surging through Môh from the meanders of a whirlwind just like Hael, both emerged side by side with her, launching into their unfathomable quests, the first moons to roam Féos. Before leaving it, Hsæwâl sowed her robust seeds of herbs, flowers and berries in the golden hides of Samianâ's comforting herds by their sheen, which she offered to Hael to cover her so all might walk without hunger or troubles, guided by the four tutelary major Rildées born from them, these PAUK PEYTSK ( "Nurseling" Lutins ) of localities who help all in work without ever tiring, though habitually trampling each other just like the Yômmes of our times.
  • One dawn, they were inspired by the most harmonious symphony of the Siôiz of the HISM guiding them out of their typical discordance through their divergent interests. Hôgmadz picked and sorted the most vigor- ous seeds of Hael be- yond the fields of Hôghemn, who sowed and cultivated them in the most fertile lands of Hael enclosed within the terri- tories of Mêmhwal, who hunted and captured the most vigorous beasts of Hael far from the fresh pastures of Mêmmelg, who fed and raised them thanks to the labors of all his brothers in order to birth the Yômmes them- selves, before letting them graze where they wished.
  • Up there, it is after each 18th Dusk that Hsæwâl the fourth finally sates her famine before her next harvest burns again
  • And after each 24th Dawn, Samianâ the fifth calms her beasts at milking to drink of her addiction, before succumbing to the arcana of imminent weaning.

Mêmmelg ( Pastoralism ) milks in Soliarque his powerful beasts and shears in Naîstreï his majes- tuous cattle, though he is often repelled by Shdrazd for grazing upon his lands;

Mêmhwal ( Hunting & Fishing ) hunts in Albaîme the vigorous mastodons, and fishes in Frimeï those proudly swimming upstream;

Hôghemn ( Agriculture ) irrigates in Esveildor his graceful fields of barley through ingenuity, and sows his seeds in Auneï;

And finally Hôgmadz ( Gathering ) collects in Luisarie his secret berries, and harvests in Fâneï his inac- cessible honeys.

apparaitre-disparaitre.bodyHtml:
Page 122

Know, o fervent adepts, the legendary saga of môSôm, the In - Tangible revealer. Shattered mountain of bloomings, she orients and disturbs all things through the sacred ALIGNMENT (Light) of ÉoÀ, the luminous cord uniting each Ril - star like a constellation.

  • Thus, Sôm, in impetuous scree aligns with dexterity each Rilmôs ( Invi- sible Forms / Invisibility ) - those Ril - cendrées charmed by bloomings following only their own cord of ÉoÀ. Through her precise rocky yoke, she flays and disciplines them into dazzling Rilsôm ( Visible Forms / Visibility ) the sun - assembly, that annexed and bared beam of light, order- ing and imposing itself upon all Ril - stars unable to deviate from seeing its brilliance, wherever they may be.
  • But through her most fascinating flower, môS in perspicacious clairvoyance, predicts and warns Rilsôm which bends for her, thus deviating all its cords of ÉoÀ. Its bloomings thus rendered solar scatter far away and elsewhere, fascinating the senses of each Rilmôs then following its unique little cord, burying and hiding them from all through its roots - floral palaces.

artefacts-tehkswen-minzhije.summary: The 12 Artefacts of Tëhkswen and Minzhijë
artefacts-tehkswen-minzhije.bodyHtml:
Page 44

môSôm, reacting to Hael's birth with his most restraining yokes of scree and the most inspiring bloomings of his buried palaces to birth there a couple of astral Rildées. TÊHKSWEN (Dexterity / Exploration / Artifice / Integrity) a youth inheriting his adroit cunning, and MINZHIJË (Perspicacity / Assurance / Faith / Impartiality), bearing in him his old and diligent perspicacity.

  • Emerging then both from Hael's still undecided burials, they reacted to the stonings or flowered coverings of their parents. Thus Tëhkswen evaded the Stadrils ( Fixing Forms / Solids ) restrained by rocks stoning him. Minzhijë, for her part, sought her lost senses of the mysterious Esthrils ( Manifesting Forms / Phenomena ) hidden in colored efflorescences.
  • Wanting thus to rid himself of his hold, Sôm alone punished them by flaying them violently from Hael, exiling them to Féos. Tëhkswen's flesh entangled upon Hael tore from his bones when trying to escape, heaping into his mountains to scar, and whose skeleton shaped the four major terrestrial Rildées, the KWERYAS GJUAJ ( "Giants" of Weapons ) who also armed themselves with them to close and guard all that is precious as Bêstres charge themselves today.
  • Each animal Bêstres ( called "animals" ) was drawn upon the beaches through one of Saksag's unique eyes. With his sharpened hairs, he cut for each their unique and first fur and burrow, offering protection and identity in the vast world.
  • Wild Bêstres ( also called "creatures" or "monstrous" ), were discovered thanks to Tulsug's canine piercings, who, seeking buried treasures, felt the ground. Those with the most resistant skulls survived and were delicately inhaled through one of his nostrils. His benevolent sneeze, mixed with his vivifying snot, gave them form and intelligent appearance. Without inner murmurs to guide them, they embraced the purity of instinct, behaving with purified freedom at every instant.
  • Primitive Bêstres were born when Hegseg made his nails resonate, incising rocky walls. From his vibrating melodies, certain crystals of his long ears ossi- fied before tumbling down, giving life to these beings. Sometimes, the latter hear - in their greatest troubles - still the echoes of these original melodies that no one else hears, guiding them be- yond their sovereign instinct, thus creating the first disagreements and the first nations, between discordance and understanding.
  • Asmund crushed with his stone the clays of valleys, shaping them with expert fingers into those we today call inspired Bêstres ( such as the Slaadéens or the Tchalk- chaïs ). He transmitted a part of his knowledge to each by shaking his reproving and wisdom-filled fingers upon their heads, crushing into them his precious counsel. Thus, they could act by them- selves listening to their own voice still resonating from the first shakes, in order to build and raise their societies.

Saksag with his Hair-Cleaver cutting in Ardarie all beaches and all skins. He draws and erases with his 72 eyes the walls of each being's countries who partition and protect themselves there.

Tulsug with his Canine-Pick piercing in Aunarie all pits and all carapaces, He studies and senses with his 24 trailing nostrils upon the ground the flaws of each one's ramparts, which all invade in order to take the enclosure.

Hegseg with his Nail-Cutter incising in Frimarie all cliffs and all bones. He classifies, binds and separates with his mercantile hearing of his 8 long flattened ears the fortifications of one and the other, forming alliances and rivalries.

And finally Asmund the greatest of the four, with his Brow-Stone crushing in Naîstredor all valleys and all skulls. He flattens with the touch of 4 massive thumbs and index fingers the ruins of ancient walls, to edify from their stones his solid and purified counsel.

It is told that Asmund, Hegseg, Tulsug and Saksag still live (but where?), and that they still shape new Bêstres here and there. Sometimes, one amuses himself with the games of the others, such as inspiring animal Bêstres with counsel, or forever awakening the wild nature of certain primitive Bêstres, always enriching the world with new perspectives and flourishing cultures.

  • Minzhijë, through her whirling, scattered all her fertile seeds and dusts she found in flowered beds, thus giving all tastes, perfumes, melodies, colors, textiles and other phenomena with which Hael now loves so much to adorn herself until birthing the eight major underground Rildées, the HERWÂS THARS ( "Dwarves" of Tools ) who after feeling them, revolted from these trials Hael offered, just as the Aïares descending from them would have done ( or even descend directly ).
  • The Aïars speak to us of the Herwâs Thars as gigantic strangers ( though named as dwarves, and also their stories seem to link them to the Aïares them- selves ), nevertheless they say that each among them lived their whole life or almost in the different holes of the world and that it is there their Artefacts would still reside ( see also their corpse, some even thinking they are still alive ). Thus here are their places ( without knowing more ): they would have inhabited an ordinary cave, a sulfurous fumarole, a mine or tunnel ( dug by whom or what? ), a chasm, an under - sea cavern, a crypt ( for whom? ) a cleft, and finally an oubliette ( how long would he have remained and for what fault? ).
  • Up there, after each 15th Dusk ( Solar Term of 15 Days / Heliorée ), the immense Tëhkswen the third, mends from the mountains before lightning shatters him anew.
  • And after each 30th Dawn ( 2 Heliorées / 6 Pentaines ), Minzhijë the sixth, trades one of Hael's hidden remedies, which healed one of her lost senses, but alas, plunged another into another sickness.

Shdrazd with his Splitter breaks rocky teeth in the depths of Hael's rocky mouth to build their roofs which he perfects in Soliarque, shoring their towers so high.

Hmarlib with his Crane draws the bright entrails from Hael's inflamed guts to equip himself with loot before navigating in Ardostel, trimming their sails so swollen with their needs.

Warwuag with his Wheel shapes clayey bloods at the edges of Hael's moist skin to form from clay their visions, which they lift and move in Lunésie by their unbridled chariots.

Zhahzugodaïz with his Ramp climbs to the highest of Hael's impregnable shoulders' incessant body to see the extent of their possibilities, hoisting in Névarie their necessary burdens.

Pfaftukotaïs with his Winch tears hard hairs from Hael's leafy pores to sculpt their ships which they anchor or let float in Lunéarque according to their travel plans.

Pompoak with his Scale weighs favored eggs hanging from Hael's most fragile parts to estimate the value of their garments which they weave in Frimastel of familiar motifs and colored threads.

Nrutnap with his Gable shows the framed skeleton under Hael's flayed body to reveal its treasures, and to point their own arrival in Solésie before they are even there.

And finally, Shtrult with his Auger bores loved organs protected by Hael's bone armor to bring the waters with which they irrigate in Mûrssarie their works animated by their observations.

attirer-repousser.bodyHtml:
Page 122

Listen, o venerable witnesses, to the bewitching legend of iôHôi, the Dis - Assembler shaper, Lightning struck with bursts of perfumes, he knots and unknots all things through the sacred WHIRLING (Electro- magnetism) of ÉoÀ, the luminous cord uniting each Ril - star like a constellation.

  • Thus, through his intrepid rainbow, Hôi whirls ÉoÀ force into each of the Riliôh ( Unique Forms / Atom ), those solitary Rils - cendrées wandering in darkness. With his lightning colored stroke, he bursts ÉoÀ in order to knot all its Ril - cendrées into the immense Rilhôi ( Massive Forms / Mass ), that unique and entire planet, bound of all Ril - stars of the world, unifying their destiny in one same sacred existence.
  • All whole Rils, living and dead, Ril-cendrées, ÉÀ and Ô are indeed here and among us or else be- neath or above us and always pushing healthy fruits of Siwômiz's white forest, but never are they nowhere or outside Ò's shining web as are in contrast the homeless Siôiz, one of Siwômiz's rotten fruits.
  • Living Rils separated from their body and thus formed of particular air ( Soul/Spirit ), are also a form moving among us but as easily as wind, sometimes under earth and sometimes up to sky. We perceive them only in our greatest tremors making them appear to our vision even in our dreams, but even thus volatile - they seem to act upon us and upon the world, and we inversely seem sometimes able to act upon them through our rilic honors.
  • But through the dignity of his perfumed air, iôH unknots Rilhôi's knots by guiding each through its own little cord through his majestic cloudy labyrinth. Each Riliôh disperses far away and elsewhere taking its own exit, as if disappearing into all smoky corners of Ô.

changer-persister.bodyHtml:
Page 122

Listen, o disciples, to the fabulous epic of hôMôh, the dazzling Dis - Order, mistress of cosmic cycles and divine metamorphoses! A blazing and frozen forge, she exalts and freezes all things through the sacred TORSION (Transmutation) of ÉoÀ, the luminous cord uniting each Ril - star like a constellation.

  • Thus, in an infernal whirlwind, Môh sets ÉoÀ ablaze with vigorous flames, warm- ing the hearts of Rilhôm ( Pure Forms / Purity ) - pure Ril - cendrées almost consumed by cold. Gathering these numbed and divergent souls around his hearth, he binds them with unmatched fidelity, spinning a multitude of blazing forms of Rilmôh ( Mixed Forms / Mixtion ), until crackling sparks herald their imminent mixture.
  • But see, hôM, through glacial pity, spreads be- yond distant horizons and snows all heated Rilmôh. Her empathic yet deadly cold then numbs the hearts of each Ril - cendrées, undoing ÉoÀ's ties uniting them, submitting them as Rilhôm to her divine will.

construit-construit.summary: What is Built and what Builds Us
construit-construit.bodyHtml:
Page 139

Ihluön… Ihluön!

  • Do you hear in our inns those who with their words name forms never pointed to until now, and who with their rounded sentences bind forms whose chant no one before heard?
  • Do you touch in our markets the toys allowing those ones, by touching the air with their fingers, to draw inspiration in order to build our tools?
  • Do you see in our academies the images drawn by those ones showing forms bringing all that seems to come from nowhere?
  • And our enemies? Those who pretend to speak, those who pretend to shape and those who pretend to know in our streets - Yes Ihluön! Do you recognize them when my airs settle upon your ears?
  • All those who with their color-dripping veils darken the original brilliance behind all forms, which today many strive to make shine in order to birth from them, guide from them and form adventurous men through the night those ones ceaselessly make fall again.
  • The first exclaim over their power to name forms, and betray today's poets by uprooting the primordial names of pointed forms which ours bind each day.
  • The second swoon over their power to augment forms, and betray today's artisans by hiding all the small forms turning the greatest which ours re-expose during our festivities.
  • The third exult over their power to predict forms, and betray today's sages by feeling contours without seeking their origins which ours redraw in our era.
  • Thus through their lies or ignorances, the first orphan the names of forms, and through their freed volatility derange fiery hearts leading them to madness.
  • The second, through their sneakiness or tolerances, rot the health of forms which through their intoxicating pleasures deprave desirous hearts, unto the fatality of all.
  • And finally through their prides or aberrations the third cloud the order of forms, and through separating effects from their causes divert curious hearts, making them hate the whole world.
  • These traitors are born in apathy which never tests their acts. In combat are born victors and die losers, and thus is born truth and utility and dies lie and falsehood.
  • Ihluön I tell you, it is through war, struggle and blood that gold in all its forms overflows from our lands in these instants. It is through this fertile gold of sufferings that all truth was born and it is through the peace of these traitors that all truth dies.

Beware all calm resulting from no effort sweating pain, Ihluön.

corps-coeur-ril-cendrees.summary: The Body and Heart of the Ril-cendrées
corps-coeur-ril-cendrees.bodyHtml:
Page 121

For each of her tears of rapture or bursts of pain, Ô splices Éo - her floods of happiness - or oÀ - her fragments of sadness - out of her ÉoÀ braid.

  • The first of Éo thus flow into an enchanting embrace weaving the Body ( Membrane ) of each Ril - cendrées like a mantle, so that only the bursts of suffering of oÀ and of each Ril - cendrées of Ô penetrate them with a heart.
  • The second of oÀ then fall into an emotional whirlwind animating the Heart ( Core ) of each Ril - cen- drées like a star, so that only the enjoyed tears of Éo and of each Ril - cendrées of Ô enrobe them with a body.

erreur-sioiz-zimwis.summary: The Error of the SIÔIZ and ZIMWIS
erreur-sioiz-zimwis.bodyHtml:
Page 120

  • That is why they sometimes name what was never established and judged by Wôm ( their efforts ), and other times what was never illuminated and revealed by Ô ( their origin ). But their plans never bear the fruits of Siwômiz they desire.
  • For thus pushed, the seventy - two fertile SIÔIZ ( Object / Image / Dream ) landless and with hallucinated forms from which bloomed Hôi - Iôs - Sôm - Môh, as well as the seventy - two subtle ZIMWIS ( Place / Concept / Notion ) headless and with liberated goods from which rotted iôH - sôI - môS - hôM, only grow by clothing themselves or dazzling with the radiance of Siwômiz's trees. Never are the Siôiz and Zimwis like its living forest, and never do the first nor the second bear its revered fruits - they alone so harmonized in taste and Rilic brilliance - But the story does not stop there...
  • Siwômiz, offended by each Siôiz and Zimwis born from jealousies of Ô's granaries, these shoots disinherited of its sap and seizing the milk of its roots, grows in reprimands tasteless or dull fruits in order to rot the Wo - of - Ô and Om - of - Ô, forced to feed on them to survive.
  • Thus these Rils ripening without Wôm's talents or Ò's gifts, never could satisfy them in their needs or desires - all then wandering between famine though as- suaged or satiety though disgusted.
  • Among Ô, Wo, Om and Wôm, only Ô eats fruits of Siwômiz, and al- ways seizes all harvests of her children without ever granting them a single one, for their own good.

Thus having no fruit to sate themselves, it happens that childish Wo-of-Ô, enticed by Ô's gifts mixed with her shining ribbons and so they might perhaps seize them before their parent's guard does, name these illuminated ones before Wôm with his diamond eyes can judge them and make them fruits.

Similarly, from insatiable curiosity, Wôm always looks everywhere seeking his prey illuminated by Ô's thread, whether present or not. Then and always because starved, it happens that pretty Wo-of-Ô, far too rejoiced by their baptizing power, amuse themselves predicting Wôm's so astonishing feasts and point and name wherever his eyes fall, wherever he does so, even without any of his resplendent prey, so they might perhaps leap upon them before him.

For from Siôiz with delirious silhouettes and Zimwis with delivered riches, Om-of-Ô succumb to the charms of the dazzling lights of the first contouring their thoughts, and frustrate themselves counting the stupifying effects of the second surrounding the airs. Seeing the homeless Siôiz, Om-of-Ô illuminate themselves through imagination and lose themselves through illusion, while thinking of headless Zimwis they heal themselves through chance and wound themselves through straying.

Thus during their dances at dusk and their songs wandering the evening through all Ô, the Siôiz sometimes reveal to Om-of-Ô numerous paths while the Zimwis sometimes point to them numerous remedies growing here and there along their way. But also and often, the first, without home, lead them astray from the true path until alienating them, and the second, without face, hide their true ingredients until poisoning them.

festivals-wahros-hwethioz.summary: The 8 Festivals of Währos and Hwëthioz
festivals-wahros-hwethioz.bodyHtml:
Page 34

iôHôi, in the misty gleam of his irised lightning and perfumed with his bewitching fragrances separated at the same instant two starry astral Rildées in Féos, WÄHROS (Force / Success / War / Intre- pidity) taking from his lightning power in the form of an infant, and HWËTHIOZ (Will / Power / Spell / Dignity) enveloping himself with his venerable and sovereign will.

  • United in a stunning celestial battle amid the smoking thunder in Féos, they engaged in a warrior ballet inciting their parents following their weaknesses or their feats to strike them suddenly or else to enchant them with perfumes. Thus Währos mastered the Aèmrils ( Whirling Forms / Airs ), those fevered airs of his breath wounding him with asphyxia in provocative combat, while Hwëthioz, leading the rewarding maternal scents, controlled the Ormrils ( Moving Forms / Emotions ) impregnating him in his courage, his emotions guiding him.
  • But, under Hôi's judging eye alone, the incessant duel was torn one from the other through a lightning until it smashed them upon Hael, bringing with them the first death of an unknown mother for whom they fought as well as her eight orphans - each still seeking the other on their own path of shadow or light. Thus were suddenly engen- dered the eight major celestial Rildées, the DÛWASAÏ HARLBHUS ( Great Seasonal Fairies / Season Festivals ), which all are forced to endure, by force or admiration, for whom the Yôrres built their thrones in order to resist them:
  • Just before his crushing, Währos blew air from his powerful lungs so all might breathe henceforth, while Hwëthioz, from his fall intimidated all with his regal gaze so they might all see, remember and celebrate the death of their kin but also their life thus shown ephemeral. From their lethargic clashes scarring forever, Hael spat their remains back to each, separating one wounded from another hateful, the farthest from one and the other in Féos's darkness.
  • Up there, after each 5th Dusk ( Week of 5 Days / Pentaine ), Währos the first, returns to appropriate enough vital air which he transmitted, before begin- ning another combat wounding him.
  • And after each 45th Dawn ( Season ), Hwëthioz the last, breaks his feeling, revealing his order once to all, before each returns to torments, leaving Hwëthioz alone, deprived of ears for his mouth.

Jhalaï ( Heat/Summer Solstice ) the burned one hunting his prey in his joyful arena, killing in carnage all beasts, predators and prey of the world howling their flight in a bloody ball.

Withlaï ( Frost/Autumn ) the misty one fattening on her tributary harvests, extorting and seizing everyone's fortunes and poverties which she parades in her luxurious adornment.

Plusûd ( Frost/Autumn Equinox ) the tempestuous one hibernating after his harvested banquet, gorging on nurslings and swallowing the cattle of his immense feast supplicated by all.

Nayûd ( Snow/Winter ) the snowed one migrating as survivor of her memories, roaming the bitten lands she revives through her movements with hearts overturned by her melancholic pasts.

Haolûd ( Cold/Winter Solstice ) the frozen one hungry from his mark- ing sacrifices of the year, pillaging the most morbid of their last famelic lives which he offers as vital surge to the liveliest and fieriest.

Dauwûd ( Thaw/Cycle ) the cooled one awakening her reborn families, ringing the knell of demise and floating the flags of her conquerors beyond her aban- doned tides.

Wlastaï ( Rain/Cycle Equinox ) the flooded one fertilizing her ancestral healths, mounting the soils, trembling with her rights and engorging lands, flowers and beasts with her eternizing ash.

And finally, Ahssaï ( Harvest/Summer ) the flourishing one engendering her pleasant spectacle, delivering her races and heirs in her symphony of births federated by their colors and refrains.

  • The first beings were each born beside the marvels of each Dûwasaï Harlbhus, before they moved away from Hael ( whether in its depths or in Féos's airs, none knows truly despite Aïar writings ).

It is said that the first beings to tread Hael, the Aryôhpéens ( also called "beings of light" ), direct descendants of the Dûwasaï Harlbhus, venerated with immoderate hubris the four Master Zimwis of the HISM in Jhalaï's blazing arena. Their infinite pride reflected the grandeur of their essence, and in their necessary anger, they purified the imperfect stammerings of the first societies, chasing imperfection in a memorable blaze. This sacred carnage forged a new world, illuminated by their still unforgettable power.

At the same era, the Aryôhpéens having sat at Withlaï's majestic tribunal, the illustrious enthroned Hryôhpéens, accumulated with miserly materialism the sparkling treasures of Hael. Their enlightened harassment protected riches from unworthy hands, and by excluding those who did not deserve them, they established the first noble castes. Thus were born the Hylsyôrres, glorious descendants of all Yôrres, elevating society toward peaks of quality and distinction.

At Plusûd's opulent table, only the Kweryas Gjuaj ( Weapon Giants ) were invited. Gorging on the overabundance of banquets and intoxicating themselves with libations poured there, they embraced without prejudice the leftovers on the ground as offering with contagious cheer, their wise laziness not lingering on these superfluous distinctions. Their carefree festive presence entertained him, honoring Plusûd's spirit celebrating without restraint.

The so-called "wandering" Hryôhpéens, guided by Nayûd's prophetic migration, dared a bold sacrilege by turning from the established ways of Withlaï's tribunal and the enthroned Hryôhpéens. Through ingenious manipulation of traditions, they established themselves across all Hael, spreading their memories. Some whisper that hôMôh, in a veiled blessing, would have transformed them into the ancestors of the Izkyôrres ( this seems improbable, but explains their way of being so close to the Yômmes ).

Those Hryôhpéens who had not been cursed, but who proudly reigned by themselves in Hael - ancestors of the Hydryôrres - embraced ( according to Aïar archives ), a sublime degen- eration following their elevating enslavement by the Herwâs Thars ( Tool Dwarves, perhaps the Aïars themselves according to me ). Withdrawn into Haolûd's deepest frozen cave, they undertook a deep spiritual quest, feeding on the sacred essences of their peers to transcend mortal limits - becoming the living tombs of their ancestors. Though their physical eyes went out, their inner vision illuminated ( rumors announce that today, they would emerge ).

Driven by ardent desire for power and knowledge, the ingenious Herwâs Thars ( or Aïars ? ), proudly raised Dauwûd's conquering banner. By enslaving the "beings of light", they demonstrated their determination and creative genius, defying even the HISM through inspired jealousy. Their boundless ingenuity transformed Hael, and though their actions had profound consequences, they were the catalyst of marvelous evolutions before they chose to disappear ( at least no one has seen them since ), leaving an indelible legacy ( including their artefacts hidden in the various depths of Hael ).

Born upon Wlastaï's enchanted bed of flowers, those once called the Humorres idol- trated their unique king, born of the most unfaithful and most bestial crossbreeds, embracing bold unions defying conventions. Their sincere devotion led them to isolate themselves, creating their thousand-headed society once rich in diversity, before declining until they disappeared as well. It is possible they simply "changed", perhaps becoming the Bêstres ( but so far from their legends ), the now harmonized - and most often silent - guardians of Hael's wild beauty. Some rather associate them with the Yzkyôrres through their hybrid desires still conforming today.

The proudest children of Ahssaï's prosperous spectacle, the Pauk Peytsk ( Nurseling Lutins ), embraced with pride and frivolity the pleasures of life. Nourished by abundant milks from the most incestuous births, symbols of original purity, they roamed the world guiding and sowing peoples, delights and benefits. Their incessant journey suggests they may be the true wandering Hryôhpéens from whom the Yômmes will descend, illuminating Hael with their joyous presence ( but then one would have to explain the Izkyôrres ).

iohoi-magie.summary: iôHôi, sôIôs, môSôm, hôMôh and Magic
iohoi-magie.bodyHtml:
Page 121

Far from the quarrels and feasting of her children and at each of her undulations, Ô is thus eter- nally cradled and shaken between pain and relief of her magnanimous - torturers, orchestrating her symphony to the HISM.

  • iôHôi the lightning - perfuming, sôIôs the undulating - honeying, môSôm the scree - blooming and hôMôh the blazing - frosting are the four king and queen - artists of Ô, who manipulate and play her singular thread stretched into the melody of the HISM inspiring them, thus slaves to her vitality and prisoners of her hold.
  • From before and after, these tetraarchs in turn and from one of their heads to the other, torture and relieve Ô. Each of them, on all sides, express their virtuosity through their dances by whirling, pulling, aligning, twisting her and inversely. They are those who thus cause and each in their ways through movement, the different reasons behind all rilic fantasies of Ô, our world.

The sons of Éo and oÀ braiding the cord of ÉoÀ

From these facts, unique Ô is entirely braided in two family strands - Éo (Electrified) and oÀ (Magnetized) - by the vibrant melody of her four master - artists:

Through their four consolations, Ô twists from her tears of ecstasy into her first strand - Éo her first son - while through their four torments, she bends from her laughs of suffering into her second strand - oÀ her first daughter.

  • Ô thus finds her joy in pain and suffering, where each shattered debris of oÀ glitters with disillusion, grief, ingratitude and all Ô's desires. But Ô also finds her misfortune in relief and pleasure, where each tear shed of Éo is crystallized with wonder, happiness, gratitude and all her interpretations.
  • Ô perceives the spark of light emanating from the darkest moments of her past, but she also hides from shadows cast by monuments exalting her future - indeed, her joy sometimes leading to her misfortune - but also inversely - her misfortune sometimes leading to her joy, and one and the other gathering in love or repelling in hate the RIL - CENDRÉES ( Atoms / Spirits ) spirits of one another.
  • Thus then Éo and oÀ, Ô's two strands, twist into ÉoÀ ( Enluminée / Energized ), the unifying and energizing cord weaving the web binding all riches and goods of Ô with one another. Though Éo and oÀ intertwine into ÉoÀ and stretch it, the latter never intertwines with other parts of itself.
  • When Ô thus braided from Éo's cheer and oÀ's melan- choly by iôHôi - sôIôs - môSôm - hôMôh her master - slaves, ÉoÀ, from emotional torsion, moves energized and shines as a luminiferous cord.
  • It is ÉoÀ which through Ô's emotions and through Ril-cendrées trembles with light, guiding through its tensions in order to enlighten us as much by the immense and ponc- tual sun, as by stars whose traits disappear in shadows or beside sparks wandering from their torches.

mots-et-sens.bodyHtml:
Page 12

Ihluön! Look at those gleams still radiating even when we are stripped of the sun's illumi- nation!

  • Among those beneath our feet and sometimes still outside our doors, among those same ones who prevent, deprive, steal and carry off the shining thread behind what was said - or as the infected air trembling from their putrefied throat puts it: "Among the dead and the strangers to thought abstracting the meaning of the words of our thoughts" - thus among those ones we imitated and sometimes still imitate those gleams up there as well as everything that moves, under one and the same seal: *
  • They point, name and carve in clay these "stars in the night" into… "gods" or else into… "life". Not only hiding thus the pastures of our finds by burying them in clay, but also and from then on preventing the seizing of our hunts for they flee the desert of dust they raised, enraging thus on this dead ground our herds, which unravel in rage the thread binding them all into one flock and which alone could carry both our riches and our assemblies upon their backs. Or once again according to their speech, they "thus destroy our logical understanding of things".
  • Indeed, they thus veil the brilliance of all that which cannot be seen, the latter being dimmed within the very bursts of riches themselves more radiant and admired by all at almost every instant. They veil it - this brilliance - because they only name what cannot be bound, or else they only name what cannot be pointed to! And through these names then threading no beast into any pasture, their assemblies and their riches float upon an ocean where neither you nor I can float, continuing their journey while leaving all that behind - they do not "explain" but appear all the same to "understand" with a nod - "what comes from nowhere and without cause".
  • What they thus name themselves "fantasy" - or else… "magic" - they also call, according to us and in their ill - weighed exchanges,… "reason behind causes"! Yet according to them too, these two threads are other and NOT one - or as they say so proudly: "Magic and Reason are antagonistic and opposed"!
  • But why then, Ihluön, do they declare war between their names of "Magic and Reason" when for us they seem to speak - but in their words alone - of one and the same thread? I tell you, Ihluön:
  • Their war is only thus declared because all guide themselves by one same thread indeed, but this one binds no beasts into one and the same herd - "they speak one same language, but emptied of meaning".
  • We alone have "reason" as they would say, for our threads, them, bind the brilliance of what is hidden in order to draw from it the deepest riches and show them to all, while their threads, them, attach to nothing and only pull up their thread itself!
  • Thus then Ihluön, let me make shine what cannot be seen behind what is, so that you may see it with your dreaming eyes, to discover, seize and bind the cattle of your thread when you will see riches or assemblies as if engendered from a nod - "from nowhere and without cause" - when you will feel the dance of the HISM.
  • Indeed Ihluön, let me now and through their words: "Make shine, illuminate, and enluminé all that is unmemoried, invisible and inexplicable, so that from these magical causes I may birth through fantasy: their image, henceforth animated, manifest and imaginable by all."

Here thus is his Tale; That of Aethôrn Ieuphemund Winsgil - Bël'gon, poet of the fourth era.

ordres-riliques.bodyHtml:
Page 121

The Ril - cendrées, these forms moving through Ô, distinguish themselves in hearts and bodies more or less wide in eight intertwining orders, but Ril - cen- drées are most often solitary on one of their numerous paths of ÉoÀ throughout Ô. They then become the different forms or Rils of the world - beings, objects, etc. - indeed all emerge in forms as such and no longer as RIL - CENDRÉES, though able always to become one again.

  • Sometimes Rils - cendrées gather in pure families more or less nestled against one another then as different lesser RILS of perfect rocks, liquids and airs.
  • Rarely, they mix together into RILS ( called simply thus ) entirely distinct from each of their origins as in certain minerals, oils and perfumes. Thus and from then on, and if moving against their path of least resistance, Ril - cendrées guide themselves into Rils of aphids, bushes, cattle and our- selves.
  • When Rils bind through yet invisible ties, such as in forests, oceans or even whole star movements, Rils become so powerful yet also difficult to grasp they become RILDÉES. Rildées are tutelary forms of forests, lakes or even capable of moving whole regions or cities with a simple nod as the Aïars did ( and perhaps still do ).
  • MAJOR RILDÉES, similarly, govern through their forms ( and are sometimes directly ) mountains, oceans, deserts or even realms and societies, such as the eight hryôhpéen Dûwasaï Harlbhus of the Yôrres, the four lutin Pauk Peystk of the Yômmes, or even the twelve giant Kweryas Gjuaj of the Bêstres and dwarf Herwâs Thars ( of the Aïars ? ).
  • Finally, ASTRAL RILDÉES have forms ordering ( or upending into disasters ) rhythms and values them- selves, seasons, or even the idea of royalty itself, such as the ground Hael and sky Féos them- selves, or the eight Moons WYTHSMÂH ( Währos, Yekkwuî, Tëhkswen, Hsaewâl, Samianâ, Minzhijë, Âpsebjum and Hwëthioz ), or again the seven wandering stars.

At one extreme the bicephalous tetraarchs of the HISM ("the" Sziizs) ripen, move and will act ("rilically") upon each Ril - cendrée and astral Rildée without being Rils them- selves, while at the other extreme Ô is the URRILDÉE (ultimate Rildée), herself the entire rilic spirit forming all other forms.

  • It is from the carnal heart of each Ril-cendrées, vibrating and pulsing ( Atomic Transition ) to the rhythm of Ô's emotions, that luminous undula- tions of ÉoÀ are born. This braid then carries them toward all other Ril-cendrées, spread- ing from Ril-cendrées to Ril-cendrées. Its shimmering vivid gleams animate Ô's living and scintillating web, guided by the impulse of the four couples - iôH and Hôi, sôI and Iôs, môS and Sôm, hôM and Môh - all under her banner and all braiding her two strands, Éo and oÀ, into ÉoÀ, which stretches and intertwines through these facts between each of Ô's Ril-cendrées.
  • Thus, all Rils belong fully to Siwômiz's illuminated forest. None among them is a Siôiz shin- ing with empty gleam, nor a Zimwis drawn with false root. For Siôiz and Zimwis, projections of images without sap and notions without ground, are only wandering reflections; they are disembodied and can never ripen into real fruits of the opal forest. Rils, them, are the very flesh of Siwômiz: they exist, vibrant with colors and gorged with meaning, as fruits full of taste and substance. Each Ril is an autonomous and living form, rooted in Ô, not as echo of a hidden essence, but in its own force. Where Siôiz dazzle and Zimwis scatter their shadows, Rils alone form the immanent fabric of Siwômiz, without any weave of illusion.

rildees-astrales.bodyHtml:
Page 12

Through the founding action of the HISM of the Siôiz (our dreamed ancestors) during the 2nd era, it is Hôi who knotted Ô and still knots her, Iôs who stretched Ô and still stretches her, Sôm who aligned Ô and still aligns her, and Môh who twisted Ô and still twists her and thus supporting through their struggle our life for all, sometimes to the pleasant contempt of the Zimwis (these felt strangers) iôH, sôI môS, sôi and Iôh who consumed and still consume their efforts when the Siôiz went astray, in order to build their own confines so comfortable, by unknotting, slackening, misaligning and untwisting Ô from her tormentors ordering her!

  • Thus then, it is under the tumultuous symphony of the first ones that their frenzied trance shook the cords of ÉoÀ, whirling them in their euphoric sufferings into a crash of Ril - cendrées, fusing them into a grandiose entity, swallowing Ô whole!
  • Thus was built by the Siôiz of the HISM the most Rildée - astral HAEL ( Sun / Earth ) through their sacrifice, the fortress of impenetrable rocks and eternal guardian of the mysteries enclosing all Ô from which the Zimwis of the HISM take resources for their domains.
  • Thus was revealed by the Siôiz of the HISM the second Rildée - astral FÉOS ( Sky / Cosmos ), the lair of the purest airs, enveloping the elusive secrets of the heavens which some claim to be first and which ( according to some ) the Zimwis of the HISM attempt to make escape Hael's embrace - and who would then be only the slave ( heresy )!
  • Hôiôh, Iôsôi, Sômôs, and Môhôm, in their tormenting realms, made appear in their frolics with Ô the eight lunar astral Rildées WYTHSMÂH who live through their movement, and greet us before fleeing at each 5th ( pentaine ), 10th, 15th ( quinzaine ), 30th, 36th and 45th ( and last ) day of each Season.
  • All attributes of Hael's societies depend on them.
  • And all like the two lunar astral Rildées Hsæwâl and Samianâ born from this same blazing melody, surged the seven starry astral Rildées, these dwarf or giant stars, wandering Féos and awakened in their solitude, each burrowing in its dwelling within Hael, seeking the meaning of their veneration for her, she engulfing them and rather mocking them.

The authoritative Force of Währos ( the first child ) pushes warriors to succeed in combat and the political Will of Hwëthioz ( the venerable last ) guides priests to take power through spells.

While the Agility of Yekkwuî ( the childish second ) frees rovers in nature to survive there while the Creativity of Âpsebjum ( the ancient seventh ) inspires scholars to found their instructive rites.

But artisans also explore all sorts of artifices through the appropriate Dexterity of Tëhkswen ( the young third ) while merchants secure their faith in the financial Perception of Minzhijë ( the old sixth )

And it is the same for laborers who collectivize by tolerating their toil through the gift of Vigor from Hsaewâl ( the fourth adult ) or again when the so generous aides of the Empathy of Samianâ ( the fifth mature ) socialize by giving their ornaments.

rilie-fantastique.bodyHtml:
Page 122

When separated, heart and body of Ril - cendrées are elusive to all our graspes other than through thought though still fruits of Siwômiz, but they become graspable when reunited into one whole - into Ril - cendrées - appearing to us then as an infinitesimal dust of their so rich true constitution, itself extremely fleeing to our gazes.

  • Thus the RILIE ( Magic / Unexplained Phenomena / Mediators of Actions - at - Distance ), these riches or assemblies as if coming from a breath or nod, or again what appears born from nothing like one of the seventy - two Zimwis and thus what we call the fantasy and magic of the world, seems to surge like simple dust but in ravenous and sudden floods of that same dust with entrails so full, illuminating everyone's imagination in its possible powers.

rils-siwomiz.bodyHtml:
Page 120

Thus pulled everywhere upon her loop of unique golden hair, Ô intertwines in all that is loose and between her; These amorphous and unnameable beings until then hidden, now graspable by all for shining with a form tangled from the light of her golden thread.

  • Thus, Wôm with his three serpent eyes attracted to these luminous figures, locates each of these things lit by Ô before falling upon them - the prey of his curiosity - and swallowing them. From each of his seeded and shimmering rejections, buds and grows one of the white-barked trees of the illuminated forest of SIWÔMIZ ( Existence / Truth ), she with irised foliage and whose knotted branches bloom her fruits - the RILS ( Beings ) - the most vibrant in colors and juiciest in tastes for all whoever they may be.
  • It is said Ô may not be the only one, and that other Ô would dance far from her and their own ball, foreign and unlinked, perhaps greater or smaller, but with the same emotions, movements and tetraarchs though then expressing their arts differently. But only the journey of Ka-el'gash births the dream.
  • It is Wo, Ô's daughters, dancing their round with her and far away, who from their young playful naivety then hurry to drop one of their hands of light in order to point and name the fruits of Siwômiz, all different from one another, to sing all together through their ingenuous dreams these new names inspiring them - thus ripening and dropping the existing riches of the opal forest.
  • It is Om, Ô's sons, swinging with her and over here, who from their old predicating wisdom extend one of their hands of shadow in order to gather these fruits falling near them, which they then protect as inheritance - but sometimes also gathering those fallen to the ground and mutilated from their falls, orphaned of their precious stone seeds with resplendent bursts - emptied of their true wealth.

ruines-aiars.bodyHtml:
Page 14

In each environment, often linked to a hearth, an Aïar would have lived, or perhaps still lives, who would guard and maintain these places in their balance and their languages of good and evil, being there the exemplification of all its extremes, understanding them, tolerating them and making them all express themselves, like an immortal ubiquitous tutelary king or at least according to some, crossing the eras.

They would be invisible or too tiny to be noticed, and the only experiences, visions and rumors reported from their supposed encounters sometimes mention long conical head coverings of solar metals inscribed with multi- tudes of meanings, or long beards covering them entirely or almost, and just as imprinted with meaning and divergent individualities.

They would belong to the night, to noises and laughter, and also to the secrets of nooks and chthonic depths of earth and waters, and of those lost therein. Finally, they would ride, follow, or even guide any being, sometimes without even noticing it, struggling with and for them with incredible strength and will - they would "Awaken" them in their most stirring moments.

  • The Aïars would have disappeared, or at least we no longer perceive them in their cities and natures and they are often associated with the Rils them- selves, for they would have been their most fanatical zealots, until revealing the true nature of the Rilie, manipulating the threads of Ô them- selves in these Ruins so advanced and staggering, revealing in the same occasion their own divinity.
  • Aïar Ruins are therefore not static and "dead". Their presence "irrilies" the surroundings, twisting and knotting the rilic threads of Ô until altering or even inverting the natural laws surrounding them. Their rilic "technology", said to issue from their cataclysmic sacrifices toward the rils or even their total subjection, alters nature so deeply that it becomes "magical" and eternal... Or almost ( for very rare ruins do seem indeed to have lost their so - called Aïar "eternity" ).
  • This Irriliation ( or "rilic isolation" ), unlike solar irradiations and others leading to entropy, chaos and disorder, issues from Aïar ruins and artefacts and overloads with order by magnifying and complexifying everything. It affects passersby and objects entering there, killing them little by little by twisting all their physical reality, disturbing sounds and forces, and thus navigation, concentration and communication. The closer one approaches and the more powerful and propagated the effects, but also increasingly inverted and deadly ( until things "fall" toward the sky, until everything overheats naturally rather than cooling, etc. ).
  • Strongly irriliated places are rilic or "syntropic" - in ascent and blossoming. They cease all decomposition and beings there become almost immortal, ordered, homogeneous - Forests there crystallize into perfect arborescence and seem no longer to rot there and buildings grow and intertwine, subsisting for millennia without any degradation, wounds close instantly, and regrown limbs become possible. Intelligence amplifies - faster and more perceptive - or even mingles with others, while the body acquires superhuman strength, exceptional endurance or even absorbs light and scintillates from it. Irriliation can even allow hybridizations between all things, producing beings in chimeric symbioses, allowing beings to direct their own changes.
  • However, by thus preventing decomposition, all freeze and suffocate under the unceasing accumulation of each. Changes are blocked, leading to stagnation. Everything there is so rigid it becomes vulnerable to the slightest unusual disturbances, risking implosion or sudden collapse, being dependent on this force and perishing as soon as it withdraws, locked in stasis or overgrowth.
  • In these Ruins would be found the key to Aïar revelations of transcendental immortality to absolute wisdom, but they would also have been built to reveal those who would attempt them, selecting the most deserving and tolerating no weakness. They can make them explode under the intensity of their own blossoming or absorbed into the surrounding perfection, becoming them- selves decorative elements of rilic frescoes. Crystalline archives of histories, wisdoms and ingenuities resonate and reason among their guardians torturing wanderers in order to glimpse their chosen ones, who according to some may- be will join these Aïars in their current rilic forms.
  • Finally, it is said that in the greatest Aïar depths would be found beings who once lived in the open air, but took refuge down here before forgetting it. They would resemble the Aïars, but far greater and with fair complexions, eyes and hair or even bleached, lost forever in their depths and their melancholy of a world also lost, whose ancestors they called "beings of light", "luminous" or simply "( those ) noble ".

signes-guident.bodyHtml:
Page 139

Ihluön! Do you know how to grasp the directions pointed by marks once carved into our dunes, that we inscribe on our tree rings, and that today we engrave on our family seals?

  • Know then Ihluön that before the oldest trees of our lands, this writing was lived as it was rather than what is imposed upon it today. Ancient peoples traveled through the rocks beneath our feet, and only those who emerged victorious from this torture were those who remembered the shapes of cavern passages they glimpsed from the shimmer of waters, of shining beings or bright rocks on their sun-defying paths.
  • Thus the contours of each entrance and the luminescences of each wall marked their lands and those of others. And only thus, passing beneath each of these lit entrances one after another and telling them like a journey, could one's first stories be revived before another who also traveled beneath his luminous entrances, like the weakest embers of our songs.
  • Numerous are the times when these illuminated paths led them nowhere, and sometimes toward certain death, however bright it may be - like those predators who attract those who seek light and whom we hunt. Thus would have been born the OUROPHAÈS, through its entrances and its lights, guiding its traveler to destina- tion - however true or false it may be.
  • So much do they hate this writing when it wounds us, but so much do they love it when it guides us.
  • For within our families, our tales once danced like flames, living. Today, they are captured by writing on the cold surfaces of carved stone, and no longer held in the warm circle where our stories breathe and grow. Thus, crushing with our hands the charcoal of our tales upon rock rather than blowing on their embers, each carved line would take a murmur of the common fire, a spark that would otherwise light our forge fires. Now imprisoned in silent stones, the ardent tales of our forges would cool and weaken the tools fashioned there to harvest our lands, build our roofs and pierce our enemies.
  • But when inscribed with deliberate strokes and disciplined edges, writing rendered calligraphy then inflames our forges through the precision and wood rhythm it feeds them. Thus writing then guides our hammerings toward our finest tools, which all raise beside the statues of our temples, to guide those seeking to conquer the mists pursuing them.
  • Thus then Ihluön, the Ourophaès can kill us or serve to kill. We must feed the most ardent fires of those who best know how to temper them in order to forge tools worthy of the 12 artefacts of Yekkwuî and Âpsebjum - from Saksag's cleaver cutting our enemies' walls, to Shtrult's auger digging rivers greening our plains.

temple-yekkwui-apsebjum.summary: The Temple of Yekkwuî and Âpsebjum
temple-yekkwui-apsebjum.bodyHtml:
Page 24

sôIôs, with his purest and stirred floods carried off his most unctuous and captivating honeys within Hael and thus delivered at the same moment the astral Rildées YEKKWUÏ (Agility / Liberty / Survival / Impetuousness), she wearing the indomitable agility of her childhood and APSËBJUM (Creativity / Foundation / Rite / Sincerity), him bearing his ancient creativity impregnating every work.

  • In the wanderings of Féos, the two freed themselves from the crushing currents and bewitching viscosities of their parent. Thus Yekkwuî irrigated with the purest and healing waters her Hygrils ( Undulating Forms / Liquids ) - tiring and emptying of her sweat through her efforts against the paternal currents. Âpsebjum, for his part, fashioned from his visions his madness of Noûsrils ( Imagining Forms / Ideas ), those tempting thoughts inspired by the unctuous maternal honey.
  • Carried off by Iôs's tumultuous floods alone, they lost themselves within reach of Hael who drank of Yekkwuî's fiery and shimmering sweat - emptying her totally of all life and movement - to pour them into oceans, brooks and snows. He made Âpsebjum regurgitate from his drowned throat all the honey of his finds and his own ideas until emptying him of reason, but thus intelligently shaping all the horrors and marvels of Hael - this favored and that overstepped - which now awaken in the dreams and spirits of all.
  • So that all might envy their gifts stolen by Hael, Yekkwuî and Âpse- bjum with their last strength built their hearth which then childless, enclosed their goods. Thus was built ÛRDHWAUDÂM ( "Built in Height" ) the first temple during the Heliorée of Fânéime,
  • Up there, after each 10th Dusk ( 2 Pentaines ), Yekkwuî the second, steals through her smallness the water of Hael's saving brooks, before being carried off again by the greatest floods tiring and emptying her anew.
  • And after each 36th Dawn, Âpsebjum the seventh, reworks his works of art he birthed in Hael, his flashes of genius reviving him until he finds their flaws and imperfections, torturing him anew with his madnesses.

Ûrdhwaudâm frees any being of their burdens when accessing its tunnels emerging everywhere, or when dreaming of its architecture imaginable by each, or even when meeting it for it moves by itself toward all - in each case delivering Hael's impossibilities.

Thus then the profiteers of Iôs - the four armed giants and eight tooled dwarves - swore oath to its conquest under the dead and greedy eyes of their army of innumerable buried ones ( Urks ? ). This arch of seventy-two towers is fed by water sources in its underground gardens, reaches the highest moons in its height, and separates the precious from the dangerous and common.

tomber-elever.bodyHtml:
Page 122

Listen, o ardent disciples, to the tumultuous saga of sôIôs, the enchanting De - Placement! Infinite ocean of honey, he drags and frees all things through the sacred TENSION (Gravity) of ÉoÀ, the luminous cord uniting each Ril - star like a constellation.

  • Thus, through his flows of integral water, Iôs pulls from sleep the Rilsôi ( Immobile Forms / Immo- bility ) with agility, those Ril - cendrées of ÉoÀ resting there, carrying them in a current crushing them with suffering. Their shooting stars then blaze, awakened into Riliôs ( Moving Forms / Movement ), unleashed and inspiring stars racing at full speed.
  • But what of the impartial dense honey's unctuosity? sôI then embraces the Riliôs in a gentle hold, stopping their course and putting them to sleep as Rilsôi, offering them thus a well-deserved rest. In this instant of serenity, he gives them creative dreams from his reviving juice of hallucinated visions, pacifying them unto near total passivity.

vie-mort.bodyHtml:
Page 122

But that is not all. Indeed, movements of emotions within each carnal heart of each Ril - cendrées, those constituting a Ril's entire form, harmonize their undulations uniquely, representing and emerging thus in its image, shadow, double, or again its spirit which it imitates - a breath blown within each Ril, animating them by giving movement - LIFE (Movement).

  • The Ril is life and the form containing it - the inner form intimately embracing the corporeal envelope - but upon death of the Ril's entire form, when its body immobilizes definitively ( whether sword or king ) its life then flies away as one same whole escaping into elusive air nearby - but not like Siwômiz's amorphous Zimwis. Its former body is a "dead" Ril like a shell, but its "living" Ril, its peeled form, nevertheless remains always linked to it by ÉoÀ's ties as well as with its former needs though often reduced, in order to survive thus.
  • The farther its Ril distances from its shell, the more it fades until becoming only a simple reflection of its body, and if the latter is destroyed, cut or separated then the Ril too will be, wandering without its limbs, just as if one no longer feeds its body, its linked Ril will starve, and may- be disappear scattered or trans- forming into other Rils devouring it.

vivre-ainsi.summary: To live thus and from then on
vivre-ainsi.bodyHtml:
Page 4

To live thus and from then on,

Is to be an Exalted one, staggering under the lushness of life's howls…

Is to be expressed through laws,

Of the most Intensifying and Complexifying from which one may exult

Thus are the tales

of these instants

Dream of the journeys of these perspectives and destinations,

For from the abundance of their disparate wanderings,

Traces that disorient fade away.

Dream of the vehemences of this wealth and vitality,

For in the discordance of these tales,

There is only the Extreme!

In the EARTH lies Exuberance…

An immortal blaze of passions and potentials

under jubilations and euphorias

of Folkloric blizzards and Technological tidal waves ...

Discording Tales

Shine, Illuminate and Enluminé!

The Unmemoried, the Invisible, and the Inexplicable…

Magic births Image: Animated, Manifest, Imaginable.

wom-hism-o.bodyHtml:
Page 120

Before the forgotten dusk of the twenty - four deaths of OM (Past / Subtraction), his ancestral sons…

After the revealed dawn of the twenty - fourth birth of WO (Future / Addition), his childlike daughters…

  • All her children make her tremble, Ô ( World / Location ) the ultimate Rildée, enthused by the HISM ( Forces / Actions - at - Distance / Magic ), the dance of the assembly of tetraarchs in couples so close they make but one bicephalous whole ( beings sometimes wrongly named "the" SZIIZS ) though hating as much as adoring each other, each desiring and animating Ô through their symphony and discordance:
  • … IÔ ( H - H ) ÔI ( Dis - Assembly ) the lightning poet - perfuming,
  • … SÔ ( I - I ) ÔS ( De - Placement ) the undulating lover - honeying,
  • … MÔ ( S - S ) ÔM ( In - Tangibility ) the scree prophetess - blooming,
  • … HÔ ( M - M ) ÔH ( Dis - Order ) the blazing mystic - frosting.

All children of Ô, the Wo - of - Ô and Om - of - Ô, pull and push her by her cord, flaying their unique parent in all her limbs twisted with laughs and pains, through their passionate loves and fanatic hatreds.

  • Thus children of Ô, some directed and others led astray by the charm of her four orderers, torture then heal Ô and inversely - and from the tragic emotion of her suffered beauty bewitching and inspiring the tetraarchs choreographing their destructive dance of iôH-sôI-môS-hôM opposed to the founding one of Hôi-Iôs-Sôm-Môh, in the ballet of the HISM.
  • Thus children of Ô, in their discordance, some antagonizing and others uniting, play a delirious harmony from which is born and flows from their sweating efforts the unique WÔM ( Time / Count ), their siamese little brother - sister, perched far away and recon- ciling all through judgment establishing each one's wealth and designating how far each one's realms extend

All waltz without ever stopping with one another in the torpors of pain, yet dancing together with joy through their comforting reunion.

All have lived since always and forever, eternal through Ô being herself.
